title: Australian Capital Territory (Self-Government) Amendment (ACT Integrity Commission Powers) Bill 2020
short_title: Australian Capital Territory (Self-Government) Amendment (ACT Integrity Commission Powers) Bill 2020

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would let the Australian Capital Territory Legislative Assembly legislate for integrity and corruption investigations concerning federal police services provided in the territory.
It would add a specific exception to the existing restriction preventing the Assembly from making laws about the Australian Federal Police's local policing services.
The change would enable territory legislation extending integrity oversight to local policing, within the limited subject matter of integrity and corruption investigations of those services.
changes: The self-government law would gain an exception to its exclusion of policing matters from the Assembly's powers.
The Assembly could legislate for integrity investigations involving federal police services delivered in the territory.
The new legislative power would also cover corruption investigations concerning those policing services.
summary.affected: The territory Legislative Assembly, its Integrity Commission and federal police providing local services are affected.

speeches.speaker: David Smith
speeches.brief: The speaker seconded a bill to amend the Australian Capital Territory (Self-Government) Act 1988, allowing the ACT Integrity Commission to investigate ACT Policing, which is currently excluded from its scope. The bill would enable the ACT government to regulate oversight of all public officials, with a memorandum of understanding expected between the ACT Integrity Commission and the Australian Commission for Law Enforcement Integrity to avoid duplication.
